newsitem.title: USA: TALBOTS EXPECTS Q2 LOSS, BACK ON TRACK H2.
newsitem.headline: TALBOTS EXPECTS Q2 LOSS, BACK ON TRACK H2.

text.p: Talbots Inc said Wednesday it expected to become profitable during the second half of the year, despite a projected second-quarter loss of $0.28 to $0.38 a share.
"We still expect to report a loss in the second quarter ending August 2 in the range of $0.28 to $0.38 a share as we announced in early July," said chief executiver Arnold Zetcher in a statement.
"We believe the loss has been confined to the second quarter and we expect to back on track during the second half of the year," Zetcher added.

Talbots' sales rose 22 percent ot $76.3 million from $62.4 million in the four weeks ended August 3. Same-store sales rose 14.8 percent over the same period, compared with a 7.9 percent decline the month before.

Zetcher, however, said the company achieved the sales "through significantly higher markdowns" compared with last year. He attributed the projected second-quarter loss to the markdowns and advertising expense.
The company said Thursday it expected to post a profitin the second half, though.
"We have worked very hard to adjust our assortment and corrected the balance between casual and classic sportswear, which we feel will better meet our customers' needs this fall," Zetcher said.
